checks.do: Which provider the account is, and the prerequisites that provider's page lists.
The Azure service principal credentials expire in one year.
Connecting AWS CloudTrail S3 buckets is described as mandatory after onboarding.

terms.statement: ZPC treats AWS accounts, Microsoft Azure subscriptions and GCP projects as cloud accounts, and AWS Organizations, Microsoft Azure tenants and GCP Organizations as organizations; multiple cloud accounts can be assigned to a business unit.

quotes: considers all Amazon Web Service (AWS) Accounts, Microsoft Azure Subscriptions, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) projects as cloud accounts.
AWS Organizations, Microsoft Azure Tenants, and GCP Organizations are considered organizations on ZPC.
Multiple cloud accounts can be assigned to a business unit.

onboarding-purpose.statement: Onboarding cloud accounts establishes the integrations ZPC needs to collect configuration and identity metadata, and multiple accounts from any cloud service provider can be onboarded.

quotes: to establish integrations required by ZPC to collect configuration and identity metadata.
You can onboard multiple cloud accounts from any cloud service provider into your ZPC service.

accounts-tab-columns.statement: The Accounts tab shows Write Access (whether remediation is enabled), Vulnerability Scan (whether scanning is configured), Status and Onboarded Date among its columns.

quotes: Write Access: Whether remediation is enabled or not for the cloud account.
Vulnerability Scan: Whether the cloud account has vulnerability scanning configured or not.
Status: The status of the cloud account.
Onboarded Date: The timestamp for when the cloud account was onboarded.

excel-export-names.statement: The cloud account, organization and Kubernetes exports are Excel files named Cloudaccounts_(timestamp), Organizations_(timestamp) and Kubernetes_(timestamp).

quotes: The downloaded Excel file follows the "Cloudaccounts_(timestamp)" naming convention.
The downloaded Excel file follows the "Organizations_(timestamp)" naming convention.
The downloaded Excel file follows the "Kubernetes_(timestamp)" naming convention.

org-onboarded-count.statement: The Organizations tab column Onboarded Accounts shows the onboarded and total number of cloud accounts in the organization.

quotes: Onboarded Accounts: The onboarded and total number of cloud accounts in the organization.

vuln-scan-script.statement: Vulnerability scanning of cloud workloads and cloud container registries needs permissions that ZPC grants through an automation script run on the cloud provider, started from Add Vulnerability Scanning.

quotes: ZPC needs permissions to perform vulnerability scanning on cloud workloads and cloud container registries.
ZPC provides an automation script to run on your cloud provider.
Select the Actions icon, then click Add Vulnerability Scanning for the cloud account you want to connect.

org-delete.statement: An organization can be deleted together with all the accounts in the organization.

quotes: You can also choose to delete an organization and all the accounts in the organization.

oci-terraform.statement: For OCI, ZPC generates a Terraform template that creates a user and group, creates a new policy allowing the group to read all resources in the tenancy, assigns the user to the group, adds a public key as the user's API key, and returns the user OCID.

quotes: ZPC provides a Terraform template that you can run on your OCI environment to onboard your OCI tenants.
Creates a new user and group.
Creates a new policy with the "Allow group attached to read all resources in tenancy" statement.
Assigns the created user to the created group.
Adds a public key as an API key for the created user.
Returns the user OCID.

oci-inputs.statement: OCI onboarding takes a Tenancy OCID (the root compartment ID), Home Region, User Name, Group Name and Policy Name; the ZPC Alias is optional and defaults to the OCI tenant name.

quotes: ZPC Alias (optional): The tenant's name on ZPC. ZPC uses the OCI tenant name if you leave this field blank.
Tenancy OCID: Unique identifier for the OCI tenant. Enter the root compartment ID.
Home Region: Home region of the OCI tenant.
User Name: User name ZPC needs to use to authenticate with the OCI tenant.
Group Name: Group name where the user is residing on the OCI tenant.
Policy Name: Policy ZPC needs to use for read permissions to OCI configuration metadata.

oci-reuse-rules.statement: For OCI onboarding, a previously created user name and group name can be entered but the user must not be assigned to the group, and an existing policy cannot be used so a new policy name must be provided.

quotes: You can enter a previously created user name and group name. However, the user must not be assigned to the group.
You cannot use an already existing policy and must provide a new policy name.

oci-user-ocid.statement: After running the Terraform template on OCI, the User OCID taken from the oci_identity_user output is entered on the Download Template page in ZPC.

quotes: Enter the User OCID generated on your OCI deployment.
Copy the oci_identity_user value.

oci-org-actions.statement: The OCI actions on the Organizations tab are Provide User OCID (the Terraform output), Provide Tenancy OCID (root compartment, used to generate the template), and Download the Template.

quotes: Provide User OCID: Enter the User OCID which is the output after running the Terraform template.
Provide Tenancy OCID: Enter the Tenancy OCID for your root compartment. ZPC uses the tenancy OCID to generate the Terraform template.
Download the Template: Download the Terraform template which you need to run on your OCI tenant to finish onboarding.

aws-prereqs.statement: Onboarding an AWS account or organization requires access to the administrative AWS management account and being a ZPC administrator.

quotes: You need to have access to the administrative AWS management account.
You need to be a ZPC administrator.

aws-two-scripts.statement: AWS onboarding uses an initial script and an onboarding script that run on AWS Cloud Shell, and supports onboarding an AWS organization or a single AWS cloud account.

quotes: supports onboarding an AWS organization or a single AWS cloud account.
ZPC provides two automation bash scripts, initial script and onboarding script, that you can run on your AWS Cloud Shell

aws-initial-script.statement: The AWS initial script creates a role named ZPC-ORG-${TENANT_HASH} and grants it the AWSOrganizationsReadOnlyAccess policy via sts:AssumeRole depending on an sts:ExternalId.

quotes: Creates a Role with name ZPC-ORG-${TENANT_HASH}.
Grants the created role arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSOrganizationsReadOnlyAccess policy via sts:AssumeRole depending on a sts:ExternalId.

aws-onboarding-script.statement: The AWS onboarding script checks it was run by the root user of the AWS management account, assigns AdministratorAccess and AWSOrganizationsFullAccess to the helper user, and creates a CloudFormation Stack and StackSet named ZPC-ORG-${TENANT_HASH} and a helper user zpc-onboarding-helper-${TENANT_HASH}.

quotes: Verifies if the script was run by the root user of the AWS management account or not.
arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess
arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AWSOrganizationsFullAccess
A CloudFormation Stack with name ZPC-ORG-${TENANT_HASH}.
A CloudFormation StackSet with name ZPC-ORG-${TENANT_HASH}.
A Helper user with the name zpc-onboarding-helper-${TENANT_HASH}.

aws-zpccustom-role.statement: ZPC creates the ZPCCustom role on all selected AWS accounts through the CloudFormation Stack and StackSet, or only the ZPCCustom role when onboarding a single AWS account, and assigns it the SecurityAudit managed policy.

quotes: ZPC creates the CloudFormation Stack and StackSet to create the ZPCCustom role on all selected AWS accounts. The script creates only the ZPCCustom role if you are onboarding a single AWS account.
Assigns the SecurityAudit managed policy to the role.

aws-cloudtrail-policies.statement: If CloudTrail is enabled, the role is assigned ZPCCloudTrailS3Access (including s3:GetObjectAcl) and ZPCCloudTrailS3AccessList (s3:ListBucket).

quotes: ZPCCloudTrailS3Access
s3:GetObjectAcl
ZPCCloudTrailS3AccessList
s3:ListBucket
evidence.after: Assigns the following policies to the role, if you enabled CloudTrail:

aws-vuln-workload-policies.statement: If vulnerability scanning is enabled, the role gets Workloads permissions ec2:CreateSnapshot*, ec2:CreateTags, ec2:CopySnapshot, ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute, kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:ReEncrypt*, kms:CreateGrant, kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext, kms:PutKeyPolicy and ec2:DeleteSnapshot.

quotes: ec2:CreateSnapshot*
ec2:CreateTags
ec2:CopySnapshot
ec2:ModifySnapshotAttribute
kms:Decrypt
kms:Encrypt
kms:ReEncrypt*
kms:CreateGrant
kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext
kms:PutKeyPolicy
ec2:DeleteSnapshot
evidence.after: Assigns the following policies to the role, if you enabled vulnerability scanning:

aws-vuln-container-policies.statement: If vulnerability scanning is enabled, the role gets Containers permissions ecr:GetAuthorizationToken, ecr:ListImages, ecr:BatchGetImage, ecr:DescribeImages, ecr:DescribeRepositories, ecr:GetRepositoryPolicy, ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability, ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer and ec2:DescribeRegions.

quotes: ecr:GetAuthorizationToken
ecr:ListImages
ecr:BatchGetImage
ecr:DescribeImages
ecr:DescribeRepositories
ecr:GetRepositoryPolicy
ecr:BatchCheckLayerAvailability
ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer
ec2:DescribeRegions
evidence.after: Assigns the following policies to the role, if you enabled vulnerability scanning:

aws-cloudtrail-mandatory.statement: Connecting AWS CloudTrail S3 buckets to ZPC is described as a mandatory step after onboarding AWS cloud accounts.

quotes: Another mandatory step after onboarding your AWS cloud accounts is to configure ZPC to collect additional configuration metadata:
Connect your AWS CloudTrail S3 buckets with ZPC to detect changes in your AWS infrastructure.

aws-cloudtrail-buckets.statement: ZPC detects the CloudTrail buckets configured for onboarded AWS accounts, may find multiple buckets for one account, and displays all of them for each account.

quotes: ZPC detects the CloudTrail buckets configured for your onboarded AWS accounts. A single AWS account might have multiple CloudTrail buckets configured. ZPC displays all the CloudTrail buckets for each AWS account.

aws-cloudtrail-kms.statement: For CloudTrail S3 buckets encrypted with a KMS key, kms:Decrypt must be assigned to the ZPCCustom role and the key policy must be modified, adding the ZPCCustom role for each member account when an AWS organization is onboarded.

quotes: If the CloudTrail S3 buckets you have onboarded to ZPC are encryped with a KMS key, ZPC needs additional permission in the KMS key policy to access the buckets.
Assign the kms:Decrypt IAM role permission to the ZPCCustom role created when you onboarded the AWS cloud account.
If you have onboarded an AWS organization, add the ZPCCustom role for each member cloud account.

aws-cloudtrail-kms-service.statement: The page tells the reader to add the S3 service and the bucket region in the kmspolicy section of the policy; its example kmspolicy statement names the services logs.us-east-2.amazonaws.com, cloudtrail.amazonaws.com, s3.<Bucket Region>.amazonaws.com and dynamodb.amazonaws.com.

quotes: In the kmspolicy section of the policy add the S3 service and the bucket region.
"Sid": "kmspolicy", "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "Service": [ "logs.us-east-2.amazonaws.com", "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com", "s3.<Bucket Region>.amazonaws.com", "dynamodb.amazonaws.com" ] }

aws-write-access.statement: Write access allows the cloud service provider to remediate alerts generated for the cloud account; once the deploy script is run, the Write Access column changes from N/A to Enabled.

quotes: The write access permission allows the cloud service provider to remediate alerts generated for the cloud account.
The Write Access column for the AWS account changes from N/A to Enabled to indicate that remediation is allowed.

aws-write-access-disable.statement: Write access for an AWS account is disabled at the policy level on AWS by removing the zpc-remediation-policy from the account's IAM role.

quotes: You can disable write access for an AWS account at the policy level on the AWS Cloudshell.
Search for the IAM Role associated with the AWS account for which you want to disable write access and then click the IAM Role from the displayed result.
On the Permissions tab, select the zpc-remediation-policy checkbox.
Click Remove.

aws-actions-aws.statement: On the Accounts tab, Add Write Access and Manage CloudTrail are listed under the Amazon Web Services actions.

quotes: Add Write Access: Enable write access for the cloud service provider to allow remediation on the cloud account.
Manage CloudTrail: Configure CloudTrail S3 buckets for ZPC to read audit trail information.

azure-prereqs.statement: Onboarding an Azure account requires being a ZPC Administrator and a Microsoft Azure Global Administrator (needed only for onboarding and revocable afterwards), access to the Root Management Group, and an Azure Active Directory premium (P1) license to view identity information in ZPC.

quotes: You need to be a ZPC Administrator.
You need to be Microsoft Azure Global Administrator.
The Microsoft Azure Global Administrator role is only required to onboard the cloud account. You can revoke this role after you are done onboarding.
Make sure you have access to a Root Management Group (the default name is Tenant Root Group).
To view identity information on ZPC, make sure you have an Azure Active Directory premium (P1) license.

azure-access-management.statement: Before onboarding, all Azure subscriptions must be made accessible by toggling Access management for Azure resources to Yes and signing out and back in to Azure.

quotes: Make sure all Azure subscriptions are accessible:
Under Access management for Azure resources, toggle to Yes.
Sign out and sign back in to Azure to refresh access.

azure-status.statement: After Azure onboarding the Cloud Accounts page shows Success when onboarding worked and metadata is collected, and Role/Resource not Found if there are issues or no resources are found in the Azure account.

quotes: verify that the status is displayed as "Success" on the Cloud Accounts page, indicating that the onboarding is successful and configuration metadata is collected.
If there are any issues or if no resources are found in the Azure account while onboarding, the status is displayed as "Role/Resource not Found."

azure-initial-script.statement: The Azure initial script creates the custom role CSP_READ_ORG with Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/descendants/read, and a service principal ZPC_${TENANT_HASH} that gets Management Group Reader, Key Vault Reader and CSP_READ_ORG.

quotes: Creates a custom role with the name CSP_READ_ORG in the subscription where the script is run.
Assigns the Microsoft.Management/managementGroups/descendants/read permission to the newly created custom role.
Creates a new service principal with the name ZPC_${TENANT_HASH} and assigns the following roles:
Management Group Reader
Key Vault Reader
- CSP_READ_ORG

azure-onboarding-script-role.statement: The Azure onboarding script creates a custom role ZPC-${TENANT_HASH} whose Actions are */read, Microsoft.Compute/disks/read and Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read, and whose NotActions are the blobServices, fileServices and queueServices read operations of storage accounts.

quotes: Creates a new custom role with the name ZPC-${TENANT_HASH} in the same subscription that the initial script was run on.
- */read
Microsoft.Compute/disks/read
Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/read
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/*/read
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/fileServices/*/read
Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/queueServices/*/read

azure-vuln-actions.statement: With vulnerability scanning permissions granted, the Azure custom role also gets the Microsoft.Compute/snapshots actions beginGetAccess/action, endGetAccess/action, read, write and delete.

quotes: If you have granted vulnerability scanning permissions, the following actions are added to the role definition:
Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/beginGetAccess/action
Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/endGetAccess/action
Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/read
Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/write
Microsoft.Compute/snapshots/delete

azure-credential-expiry.statement: The page says the onboarding script creates a service principal and that its credentials expire in one year, and ZPC continues metadata collection for the Azure account only after new credentials are provided in the ZPC Admin Portal.

quotes: The onboarding script creates a service principal that ZPC uses to collect Microsoft Azure configuration metadata.
The service principal credentials expire in one year.
When these credentials expire, you need to create new credentials and provide them on the ZPC Admin Portal.
ZPC can continue metadata collection and offer security posture for your Azure cloud accounts only after you update the credentials.

azure-credential-reset.statement: The page resets the service principal credentials with az ad sp credential reset, whose example sets --years=2.

quotes: az ad sp credential reset --id "<Service Principal ID>" --query=[appId,password] --years=2 --out json

azure-sp-name.statement: The service principal ID is found by display name ZscalerCollector-, or by display name ZPC_ for cloud accounts onboarded after January 2023.

quotes: az ad sp list --display-name "ZscalerCollector-" --query "[0].appId" --out tsv
If you have onboarded your cloud account after January 2023, run the following command to find the service principal ID:
az ad sp list --display-name "ZPC_" --query "[0].appId" --out tsv

azure-graph-roles.statement: The Azure page lists these Microsoft Graph roles with IDs: Application.Read.All, AuditLog.Read.All, Directory.Read.All, Reports.Read.All and UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All.

quotes: Microsoft Graph roles:
| Application.Read.All | 9a5d68dd-52b0-4cc2-bd40-abcf44ac3a30 |
| AuditLog.Read.All | b0afded3-3588-46d8-8b3d-9842eff778da |
| Directory.Read.All | 7ab1d382-f21e-4acd-a863-ba3e13f7da61 |
| Reports.Read.All | 230c1aed-a721-4c5d-9cb4-a90514e508ef |
| UserAuthenticationMethod.Read.All | 38d9df27-64da-44fd-b7c5-a6fbac20248f |

azure-aad-graph-roles.statement: The Azure page lists these Azure Active Directory Graph roles with IDs: Azure Active Directory Graph, Directory.Read.All and Policy.Read.All.

quotes: Azure Active Directory Graph roles:
| Azure Active Directory Graph | 00000002-0000-0000-c000-000000000000 |
| Directory.Read.All | 5778995a-e1bf-45b8-affa-663a9f3f4d04 |
| Policy.Read.All | 6c2d1b1d-a490-4178-ba6b-7efceda9129b |

gcp-prereqs.statement: Onboarding a GCP account requires being an administrator, having the GCP owner role, and having the Cloud Assets API enabled on all GCP projects.

quotes: Be an administrator.
Have the GCP owner role.
Make sure all GCP projects have the Cloud Assets API enabled.

gcp-initial-script-apis.statement: The GCP initial script enables API services for ZPC on each selected project, including cloudresourcemanager and orgpolicy.

quotes: Enables the following API services for ZPC on each selected project:
cloudresourcemanager
orgpolicy

gcp-initial-script-sa.statement: The GCP initial script creates a service account ZPC-${TENANT_HASH} in the project where it is run and binds roles/browser, roles/iam.organizationRoleViewer and roles/resourcemanager.folderViewer at the organization level, plus roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator and roles/iam.securityReviewer on the ZPC service account.

quotes: Creates a service account with the name ZPC-${TENANT_HASH} in the GCP project where the script is run on the GCP Cloud Shell.
roles/browser
roles/iam.organizationRoleViewer
roles/resourcemanager.folderViewer
roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator
roles/iam.securityReviewer

gcp-onboarding-script.statement: The GCP onboarding script grants roles/viewer, roles/cloudasset.viewer, roles/bigquery.dataViewer and roles/actions.Viewer for the organization, folders or projects, and creates a custom role ZPC_${TENANT_HASH} with the storage.buckets.get permission.

quotes: roles/viewer
roles/cloudasset.viewer
roles/bigquery.dataViewer
roles/actions.Viewer
Creates a custom role with the name ZPC_${TENANT_HASH} and assigns it the storage.buckets.get permission.
Updates the following permissions for the service account for the entire organization, folders, or projects:

gcp-vuln-roles.statement: With vulnerability scanning enabled, the GCP service account additionally gets roles/containerregistry.ServiceAgent and roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter.

quotes: Assigns the following additional roles to the service account, if you have vulnerability scanning enabled:
roles/containerregistry.ServiceAgent
roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

gcp-grant-consent.statement: After the GCP script runs, clicking Grant Consent to Service Account allows the service account to collect configuration and identity metadata.

quotes: After the script successfully runs, click Grant Consent to Service Account. This allows the service account to collect configuration and identity metadata.

aws-custom-policies.title: The AWS custom policy list
aws-custom-policies.detail: The AWS onboarding page lists about 200 service:Action permissions under "Custom Policies" (lambda, apigateway, dynamodb and others); only the structure is known here and the list stays in the capture.

azure-credential-lifetime.title: What lifetime an Azure credential reset grants
azure-credential-lifetime.detail: The page says the service principal credentials expire in one year, while the reset command it shows uses --years=2; the lifetime a reset grants is not stated as a rule.

azure-graph-tables.title: What the Azure Graph role tables are assigned to
azure-graph-tables.detail: The tables are not tied to a sentence naming what they are assigned to; the page says "Assign the following predefined Microsoft Azure read-only roles to the Service Principal: - See roles." That the Graph roles are those roles is not stated.

gcp-api-list.title: The full list of APIs the GCP initial script enables
gcp-api-list.detail: The page lists admin, apikeys, cloudasset, cloudresourcemanager, iam, monitoring and orgpolicy, but short names fall under the quote minimum, so only part is quoted.

write-access-beyond-aws.title: Whether Azure, GCP or OCI accounts have write access
write-access-beyond-aws.detail: Add Write Access is listed only under Amazon Web Services and the write-access article covers AWS only; whether other providers have write access is not stated.
